slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed code primarily performs extensive imports and compatibility handling for network-related modules across Python 2 and 3 versions. It sets up aliases and type definitions to enable network communication functionality in a cross-version manner. There is no evidence of executing remote code, obfuscated exfiltration, or system manipulation. Unlike the known malicious patterns, it does not fetch or execute remote scripts, install packages, decrypt payloads, or send environment data to external servers. malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate tools implement auto-updating mechanisms, but these are always opt-in, well-documented, and never execute remote code automatically at import-time.

malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate utility package should not install arbitrary dependencies, enumerate user directories, manipulate cryptography libraries, or execute encrypted code at import-time.
